items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: I did study privately with a man named Bob Bianco, who was a great, great teacher and wonderful influence.

ctx.x: Well he said you take the four part chord and drop the alto part an octave lower basically, and there’s your drop two voicing. And I went, “oh my God, this opens up a whole nother world.” And I did study privately with a man named Bob Bianco, who was a great, great teacher and wonderful influence. I studied privately with him out in Queens, the Schillinger System of Musical Composition.
Oh my, I’ve heard that word a lot.
